top_choice_rationale: Base editing is a defined nucleobase deamination placed under programmable control, quantified as efficiency, product purity, bystander and off-target deamination, reproduced in many laboratories and now entering the clinic. The adenine editor required evolving a deaminase to act on DNA, a separate chemical problem from the cytosine editor, so Liu, Komor and Gaudelli match the two experimentally demonstrated results. A citation naming the base conversion, not RNA-guided cleavage, separates it from the 2020 prize. P001 is my second choice because reversible-terminator chemistry is real nucleotide chemistry, but it splits the sequencing credit and leaves Komor and Gaudelli out.
